audit.why: Comet Spear is 575 range at 11s rank 1 and Shield Vault 600 at 13s, so his threat is real but slow and short — you hold 1075 on Q. From 6 the ultimate maths decide it: Grand Starfall is 180s against Chronobreak's 110s, and Ekko takes 52.73% over 1081 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: The three decisive interactions were all absent. Aegis Assault is a channel, so your Parallel Convergence stun cancels it outright; it also makes him invulnerable to damage from the front, so a string thrown into it does nothing; and Shield Vault carries an auto-attack reset, meaning the wind-up rather than the cast is the tell.
audit.why: enemyKit E flags: shield, untargetable, channel (interruptible — any CC cancels it); E text: invulnerable to damage from the front. enemyKit W flags include autoReset. These are exactly the three missingInteractions rules for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns, dos and don'ts now say to cancel Aegis Assault with the W anomaly rather than damage it, to attack from behind him if you cannot, and to read the Shield Vault wind-up.

edits.before: Pantheon is built to dominate exactly this early stretch — his Comet Spear has long range and heavy poke, and Shield Vault stuns you into a full combo with very little counterplay at levels 1-2. Play maximally passive, staying behind minions and avoiding his spear angle entirely; any hit sets up a stun-into-kill sequence. Levels 3-5 don't improve much for you since his stun-combo damage still out-trades your slower-scaling kit — your job here is purely to survive and not feed his snowball, not to contest CS aggressively.
edits.after: Pantheon front-loads this stretch, but his reach is shorter than the page implies: Comet Spear is 575 and Shield Vault 600, against your 1075 on Q. Stay outside 600 and levels 1-2 are even — inside it, the Vault opens off an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is your cue to leave, not the cast. Levels 3-5 hinge on one read: the 13s after Shield Vault is your window for the full string, and the 13s before it is his. Aegis Assault (22s) is his answer, and it only blocks damage from the front.

edits.before: Level 6 gives Pantheon global pressure via Grand Skyfall, meaning even when he's not in lane he can threaten your team's side lanes or set up jungle plays — ward accordingly and communicate his ult status. Your own level 6 at least gives you Chronobreak as an answer if he dives in for a kill, letting you survive the stun-combo and punish the follow-up. Continue playing for scaling rather than contesting him directly; look for roam windows once he's forced to shove or back.
edits.after: Level 6 gives Pantheon Grand Starfall at 5500 range, so he can leave lane to decide a fight elsewhere — ping it the moment it is spent, because it is 180s at rank 1 and he is a normal melee champion for all three of those minutes. Chronobreak is 110s, so your ultimate is back well before his. That gap is the lane: play the cycle where you hold a rewind and he holds nothing, and take your windows in the 13s after each Shield Vault.

The second suspectName, 'Use Shield Vault' in wants.foe[1], is a FALSE POSITIVE — Shield Vault is the correct name for the W; I rewrote that line for the auto-reset tell rather than for the name.
